implementation_notes: Scala's concurrent map does the create-or-return: a companion object holds a scala.collection.concurrent.TrieMap[K, T] and getOrElseUpdate(key)(create(key)) computes the value for an absent key; the Scaladoc states the thunk is invoked at most once, and that it may be invoked without the result being stored when another thread wins the race. A private constructor plus the companion accessor close construction; a plain mutable.HashMap's getOrElseUpdate is not atomic and would need an explicit synchronized block.
pitfalls: TrieMap.getOrElseUpdate may evaluate the thunk even when another thread is inserting the same key (the result is then discarded), so side-effecting construction must tolerate a speculative run.
mutable.HashMap + getOrElseUpdate gives no atomicity guarantee at all; the concurrent collection was the point.
The companion object is per class loader and the instances are never collected: per-request keys leak even though TrieMap's own structure is memory-efficient.
